newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Petron to adjust oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Petron to adjust oil prices.

text.p: Oil refiner Petron Corp will adjust prices of various petroleum products on February 8 when the government implements full deregulation of the oil industry, company sources said on Thursday.
The wholesale posted price of premium gasoline will be raised by 41.31 centavos per litre while unleaded premium gasoline will be increased by 0.59 centavos, they said.
Wholesale price of liquefied petroleum gasoline will be raised the most by 62.36 centavos per litre.
But wholesale posted prices of other petroleum products will be cut.
Regular gasoline will be reduced by 2.80 centavos, aviation turbo by 19.23 centavos, kerosene by 8.65 centavos, diesel by 16.12 centavos and fuel oil by 11.22 centavos a litre.
Wholesale posted prices refer to the cost of petroleum products from the depot less the dealers or haulers charge.
The government has set February 8 as the date when the country's oil sector, which has been under state control for over two decades, will be completed deregulated.

The deregulation programme, a part of President Fidel Ramos' economic reforms agenda, has been implemented since August last year when the government began dismantling controls on marketing and prices of petroleum products.
To cushion the impact of deregulation, the government decided to implement it in phases and full decontrol, earlier set for March, has now been advanced to February 8.
Industry officials had said full deregulation of the industry was expected to usher in local price wars and heightened competition.

On Thursday, four opposition legislators filed a petition in the Supreme Court to halt the government from going ahead with full deregulation saying the government had no authority to advance the date.
Court officials said there was no word yet on when the petition might be considered.
